transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because something happened at work. I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch before the approvals were actually in place. I committed company money and vendor time, and at the time it felt bold and necessary, like I was doing the right thing.

But now I’m on leave, and everyone’s asking what I was thinking. Honestly, I’m asking myself that too.
During that time, were you needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling full of energy?
I’m not really sure. I wasn’t keeping close track of my sleep then. I know I was pushing hard, but I can’t say clearly that I needed less sleep or felt unusually energized.
During that time, did you have any beliefs that other people said were not true or unrealistic?

I don’t know. I mean, people definitely told me my plan wasn’t realistic, or that I was moving too fast. But I’m not sure I had, like, a belief that wasn’t true. I thought I was making a strong business call. Now I can see maybe I was overconfident, but I’m not sure beyond that.
During that time, did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or on top of the world?

Yes. I wouldn’t say “euphoric” exactly, but for the past few weeks I felt sort of brilliantly alive, like I could finally show leadership what HR could be.

And then if someone questioned me, even about small edits or normal budget questions, I’d get suddenly furious. It felt way bigger than it should have.
During this period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life, like major trouble at work or in your relationships?

Yes. It’s caused real problems at work. Because of how I handled the launch and the arguments around it, they put me on administrative leave. And now I’m not trusted to manage the HR projects I was leading before.
During that period, did you hear or see things that other people could not?
No, I don’t think so. I didn’t hear voices or see anything that wasn’t there, at least not that I noticed. It was more my mood and my confidence were way up.
During that time, were you talking much more than usual?

Yes. In meetings especially, I’d hear myself talking way faster and going on much longer than I normally would. I’d jump from employee engagement to gallery layouts to retention metrics, and people would basically have to cut in or raise their hands to get me to stop.
During that time, did you feel you had special abilities or unusually important powers that other people did not have?

I’m not sure I’d say special powers. I felt unusually sure of myself, like I understood what needed to happen better than other people did, but I didn’t think I had some kind of ability nobody else had.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I’ve had low days, sure, but I can’t think of a clear stretch of two weeks where I was depressed or lost interest in almost everything nearly every day.
During that time, were you taking on a lot more projects or activities than usual?

Yes, definitely. I was trying to handle way more at once than I normally would — the HR redesign, reaching out to gallery partners, contacting festival organizers, and trying to fix several staff conflicts all at the same time. It felt like every idea had to be acted on right away.
Before this recent period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually high, irritable, or overconfident in a similar way?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I was stressed or more confident than usual, but nothing that really stands out to me as the same kind of thing as this recent period.
During this period, did you believe something with complete certainty that other people said was impossible or clearly untrue?

No, I don’t think so. I had strong opinions and I was pretty sure I was right about a lot of things, but I don’t remember believing something that other people said was impossible or obviously untrue.
